'''''Bletilla striata''''', known as '''hyacinth orchid'''<ref name = RHSPF /> or '''Chinese ground orchid''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the orchid family Orchidaceae, native to Japan, Korea, Myanmar (Burma), and China ([[Anhui]], [[Fujian]], [[Gansu]], [[Guangdong]], [[Guangxi]], [[Guizhou]], [[Hubei]], [[Hunan]], [[Jiangsu]], [[Jiangxi]], [[Shaanxi]], [[Sichuan]], [[Zhejiang]]).<ref name="q">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=22655 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200028535 Flora of China v 25 p 210, 白及 bai ji, ''Bletilla striata'' ]</ref> It is most commonly found growing in clumps alongside grassy slopes with sandy soil.<ref name=JFlora>Ōi, Jisaburō. ''Flora of Japan'' (English translation). The Smithsonian Institution, 1965</ref>

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''striata'' means "striped", in reference to the ribbed leaves.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

== Description ==

''Bletilla striata'' is a terrestrial orchid with pleated, spear-shaped leaves. It breaks dormancy in early spring, with each tuber of the previous year potentially sending out multiple shoots. These growths mature over the course of a couple months and eventually bear 3-7 magenta-pink flowers.<ref name = MOGardens/>

== Cultivation ==

In cultivation in the [[United Kingdom|UK]] it is hardy in sheltered locations down to {{convert|-10|C|F}}. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web 
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/2323/i-Bletilla-striata-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Bletilla striata''
| accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref>

In the U.S. it may be grown in [[Hardiness zone#United States hardiness zones (USDA scale)|USDA hardiness zones]] 5–9, although a winter mulching for plants grown in zone 5 is recommended.<ref name = MOGardens>{{cite web
| url= https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283860&isprofile=0&
| title = MO Botanical Garden - ''Bletilla striata''
| accessdate=18 December 2018}}</ref> 

Like most terrestrial orchids, it drops its leaves as it enters winter dormancy; however, it tolerates moisture during this period much better than most others. Nevertheless, it is encouraged to grow ''Bletilla striata'' in a well-draining, humus-rich mix.<ref name = Phytesia>{{cite web
| url = http://www.phytesia.com/en/cultivation-how-to-grow-hardy-orchids.php?genre=1
| title = Phytesia - ''Bletilla''
| accessdate=18 December 2018}}</ref>

== Uses ==

''Bletilla striata'' is used in Asian [[traditional medicine]] for problems with the lining of the alimentary canal, such as ulcers.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Chunming Wang |author2=Jiantao Sun |author3=Yi Luo |author4=Weihua Xue |author5=Huajia Diao |author6=Lei Dong |author7=Jiangning Chen |author8=Junfeng Zhang |pmid=16614890|year=2006|title=A Polysaccharide Isolated from the Medicinal Herb Bletilla striata Induces Endothelial Cells Proliferation and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Expression in vitro|volume=28|issue=8|pages=539–543|doi=10.1007/s10529-006-0011-x|journal=[[Biotechnology Letters]]|s2cid=21034616 }}</ref>{{npsn|date=September 2024}}

It is also used as a natural glue for making silk strings for [[traditional Chinese instruments]] such as the [[guqin]].<ref>{{cite book | title = Yu-Ku-Chai translation | volume = 3 | chapter = Chapter 9: The Method for Making Strings | url = http://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~jrb/chin/v39/v39.htm }}</ref>
